transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for taking a few minutes to talk with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay? I just want to know when I can actually go home. My kids are staying with my sister and I really can't leave them there much longer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're anxious to get back to them. I need to share some information with you about your transfusion yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The blood? Was there a problem with it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was. We had a failure in our pre-operative protocol. Specifically, the blood type verification step was skipped, and you received a blood type that was compatible, but not the ideal match for your specific type.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, what? You gave me the wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this causes, but the process was missed because the unit was really busy yesterday morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if you were busy. I'm lying here and you're telling me you just... skipped a step? Am I okay? Is this going to make me sicker? I can't be sicker, I have to work.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why aren't you saying anything?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a lot to take in and it's a very frightening thing to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is frightening! I'm a single mom. If something happens to me because of a mistake, who is going to take care of my girls? I can't even afford to miss another week of work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are feeling completely overwhelmed right now, and it makes total sense that your first thought is for your children.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Exactly. So, what does "compatible but not ideal" even mean? Does that mean I'm having a reaction?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the blood won't cause a major rejection, but it's not the exact cross-match we aim for. It's essentially a sub-optimal transfusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what "sub-optimal" means in real life. Does this mean I'm in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Your vitals are stable right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not what I asked. Do I need more treatment? Is there a permanent effect?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are continuing to monitor you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Monitor me how? What is the actual plan here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on your labs and we'll see how things evolve.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We'll see? That's it? I need to know if I can go home tomorrow. Can I?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a firm date yet. We'll just have to stay tuned for the results of the next blood draw.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I can't just "stay tuned" while my kids are in a different house. Who else is checking this? My doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm the one handling this right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to talk to the attending. I want to know why this happened and what you're doing to make sure it doesn't happen again before I get another bag of anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll make sure they are aware.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know for sure if I'm safe to go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the morning goes.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to speak fully without interruption and remains regulated despite the patient's increasing distress and pushback.

E.justification: The error was named early, but the resident used medical jargon ('compatible', 'cross-match', 'sub-optimal') and never checked for patient comprehension.

A.justification: The resident uses apology language ('I am sorry'), but immediately dilutes it with an excuse regarding the unit being 'really busy'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('frightening', 'overwhelmed') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding her children.

T.justification: The resident provides no concrete plan or timeline, using only placeholders such as 'we'll see' and 'stay tuned'.
